steps.reveal: Someone asks to use your authority
Someone asks to use your authority

sheets.title: Settings › Capabilities, Notifications off (the default) — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: The Notifications section now carries two optional capabilities, so it draws a tile for each; both start off, and nothing of notification routing is loaded.
sheets.after: #feature-notifications: 3 switches (section + Push notifications + Notification routing), 2 tiles, all off

sheets.title: Switched on, after the consent review's Apply — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: The section switch proposes both capabilities; Apply records the consent receipt and the plan approves them. Only then is the module loaded.
sheets.after: 3 switches aria-checked=true: the section, Push notifications, Notification routing

sheets.title: Settings › Notifications: channels and destinations — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: A new Settings category. The Channels panel carries ADR 0084's standing sentence, each channel's capability from os-domain's closed record and a status glyph; Destinations lists the bound Telegram with no provider subject.
sheets.before: /settings/notifications falls back to General (Appearance, Locking, Keybindings); 5 settings tabs
sheets.after: 6 settings tabs (Notifications current, 109×44); 4 channel rows, 1 destination row; head keys 44×44; .note 0

sheets.title: Each kind of request's order — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: One panel per notification class: order rows with the route's verdict as a glyph, move/remove keys, and an Add select that offers only what policy allows for that class. A request you sent gets decided still lists Push from before policy tightened: its glyph is the policy refusal.
sheets.after: order keys 44×44; Add select 308×44; marks include “Your operator's policy does not allow this kind of prompt to go here…”

sheets.title: The settings file in the file viewer — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: The open-file key on a panel head opens settings/notifications/routing.json; channels.json and bindings.json sit beside it, read-only (lock glyph). There is no config.yaml: every setting here lives in the provider's files.
sheets.before: no such file: the address stays /settings/notifications
sheets.after: ?file=settings/notifications/routing.json; files: routing.json, channels.json (lock glyph), bindings.json (lock glyph)

sheets.title: A refused preference: the file adds Push where policy refused it — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: Adding native_push to authorization_request in the file is checked against the route the Identity API reported for that class. The refusal is the StatusMark's sentence, the textarea is aria-invalid and Save is disabled; nothing is sent.
sheets.after: mark: “Your operator's policy does not allow Push notification for "Someone asks to use your authority". A preference can reorder and narrow what policy allows; it cannot add to it.”; textarea[aria-invalid=true] 1; Save disabled 1; no PUT in the stand-in's log
